dataStatus: DRAFT: pending clinician sign-off. Values were transcribed from the sources below; several primary texts could not be accessed (see each source note).

sources.name: 2022 American Society of Anesthesiologists Practice Guidelines for Management of the Difficult Airway
sources.publisher: American Society of Anesthesiologists (Apfelbaum et al.)
sources.accessNote: Full guideline text not accessed in this build. Principles (oxygenation, capnography, limiting attempts, escalation) confirmed from APSF/commentary summaries. No numeric attempt limit is encoded. Audit 2026-11: no newer ASA edition found. The separate Difficult Airway Society 2025 guidelines (Br J Anaesth 2026;136:283-307, doi 10.1016/j.bja.2025.10.006) exist; only their abstract was read and they are not used here.

sources.name: ASRA Checklist for Treatment of Local Anesthetic Systemic Toxicity (2020 version)
sources.publisher: American Society of Regional Anesthesia and Pain Medicine (Neal, Neal, Weinberg)
sources.accessNote: Primary text returned HTTP 403 in this build. Lipid dosing (100 mL bolus then 250 mL over 15-20 min for >70 kg; 12 mL/kg ceiling; repeat bolus / double infusion) is corroborated by UCSF and APSF summaries and by the project specification. Weight-based (<70 kg) figures come from the specification. Audit 2026-11: still the latest published checklist per a web search, which also reports that ASRA has a review in progress.

sources.name: MHAUS: Managing a Malignant Hyperthermia Crisis / Dantrolene Administration After an MH Event
sources.publisher: Malignant Hyperthermia Association of the United States
sources.accessNote: MHAUS dosing page not retrieved directly. Initial 2.5 mg/kg and repeat-until-controlled are corroborated by secondary reviews; the 10 mg/kg cumulative figure is confirmed on the Ryanodex and Revonto labels.

sources.name: Recognising and managing a malignant hyperthermia crisis (v2024)
sources.accessNote: EMHG page excerpt confirms the 2024 revision updated dantrolene dosing but did not show the figures. A secondary summary gives 2-2.5 mg/kg initial; NOT encoded because it could not be verified. Obtain the full text before relying on EMHG figures. Audit 2026-11: v2024 is still the current crisis guideline per a web search.

sources.name: An Official ATS/ESICM/SCCM Clinical Practice Guideline: Mechanical Ventilation in Adult Patients with ARDS
sources.publisher: American Thoracic Society / ESICM / SCCM (Fan et al.)
sources.version: Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2017;195:1253-1263
sources.accessNote: Recommendation (tidal volume 4-8 mL/kg PBW and plateau pressure below 30 cmH2O) confirmed from guideline summaries. The 6 mL/kg default and "<= 30" wording come from the project specification and the ARDSNet trial. Audit 2026-11: a 2024 ATS update exists (Qadir et al., Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2024;209:24-36, doi 10.1164/rccm.202311-2011ST; abstract read). It adds recommendations on corticosteroids, VV-ECMO, neuromuscular blockers and higher PEEP, and its abstract lists no new tidal-volume or plateau-pressure question.

sources.name: Guidelines to the Practice of Anesthesia: Revised Edition 2025
sources.accessNote: Only the 2023 edition wording (total cumulative local anesthetic dosage should be discussed and documented) was seen; not confirmed for 2025. Audit 2026-11: these guidelines are revised yearly and a Revised Edition 2026 is listed by the CAS (Can J Anesth vol 73 no 1); it was not read.

sources.name: Maximum Recommended Doses of Local Anesthetics: A Multifactorial Concept
sources.publisher: Rosenberg PH, Veering BT, Urmey WF. Reg Anesth Pain Med
sources.accessNote: Full text read. Table 1 lists the official US maxima (PDR 2004): bupivacaine 175/225 mg, lidocaine 300/500 mg, mepivacaine 400/550 mg, ropivacaine 225 mg (300 mg brachial plexus), chloroprocaine 800/1000 mg; and cites bupivacaine 2 mg/kg (FASS Sweden / Pharmaca Fennica 2004). The authors state these limits are not evidence-based.

scope: routine fasting intervals: clear liquids, breast milk, formula, nonhuman milk, light meals, fatty meals

sources.accessNote: Open-access guideline. Table 1 and the fasting recommendations were reviewed. Sodium citrate non-particulate antacids (30 mL 0.3 M) increase gastric pH; H2RA and metoclopramide reduce volume and increase pH.

sources.name: 2023 American Society of Anesthesiologists Practice Guidelines for Preoperative Fasting: Carbohydrate-containing Clear Liquids with or without Protein, Chewing Gum, and Pediatric Fasting Duration
sources.publisher: American Society of Anesthesiologists (Joshi et al.)
sources.accessNote: Relevant recommendations and scope read via publisher-indexed full text. Reaffirms clear liquids up to 2 h; carbohydrate-containing clear liquids may be used; protein-containing clear liquids are not preferred; evidence is insufficient to choose 1 h over 2 h in children; gum should be removed before anesthesia.

sources.name: Peri-operative fasting in adults: an international, multidisciplinary consensus statement
sources.publisher: International multidisciplinary stakeholder panel (Rüggeberg et al.)
sources.accessNote: Open-access full text via PMC. Eight Delphi recommendations; not formally endorsed by a single society. Scope is adult elective anesthesia/sedation, excluding procedure-specific fasting and conditions that substantially increase aspiration risk.

sources.name: American Society of Anesthesiologists Consensus-Based Guidance on Preoperative Management of Patients (Adults and Children) on Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) Receptor Agonists
sources.accessNote: Official ASA guidance read. Suggests considering holding daily GLP-1 on the procedure day and weekly GLP-1 for 1 week before; standard fasting applies; urgent or emergent cases are treated as full stomach. The page now points to newer multisociety guidance.

sources.name: Preprocedure Care of Patients on Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists: A Multisociety Clinical Practice Guidance
sources.publisher: American Society of Anesthesiologists, AGA, ASMBS, ISPCOP and SAGES
sources.accessNote: Official ASA release and article metadata read; full guidance not accessed. Most patients continue GLP-1 therapy; selected higher-risk patients may need a 24 h liquid-only diet, aspiration-plan changes, gastric ultrasound or delay.

sources.name: Perioperative management of patients taking glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists: SPAQI multidisciplinary consensus statement
sources.publisher: Society for Perioperative Assessment and Quality Improvement (Oprea et al.)
scope: GLP-1 solid and clear-liquid fasting protocol
sources.accessNote: Open-access full text. Separate protocol: continue if no significant GI symptoms; solids 24 h; clear liquids <10% glucose 4 h and >=10% glucose 8 h. These times conflict with other society guidance; do not combine protocols.

sources.name: Elective peri-operative management of adults taking glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide agonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors
sources.publisher: Association of Anaesthetists, CPOC and UK multidisciplinary societies
sources.accessNote: Open-access full text. Continue GLP-1 and dual GIP/GLP-1 therapy; follow standard fasting; do not extend fasting for the drug alone. Upper GI symptoms alone do not determine gastric content; consider individualized aspiration precautions and gastric ultrasound.

sources.name: Clinical Practice Recommendations regarding patients taking GLP-1 receptor agonists and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor co-agonists prior to anaesthesia or sedation for surgical and endoscopic procedures
sources.publisher: Australian Diabetes Society, ANZCA, GESA and NACOS
sources.accessNote: Full PDF and published version reviewed. Do not routinely stop therapy; recommend a 24 h clear-fluid diet then a standard 6 h fast for all patients on these drugs. Risk mitigation is required if solids were not withheld for 24 h.

sources.name: Practice Guidelines for Obstetric Anesthesia
sources.publisher: American Society of Anesthesiologists and Society for Obstetric Anesthesia and Perinatology
sources.accessNote: Official PDF excerpts reviewed. For uncomplicated elective cesarean delivery, moderate clear liquids may be allowed up to 2 h and solids should be fasted for 6-8 h depending on fat content. Audit 2026-11: no newer edition found in a web search.

sources.name: Statement on Oral Intake During Labor
sources.publisher: American Society of Anesthesiologists Committee on Obstetric Anesthesia
sources.accessNote: Full statement read. Avoid solid food in active labor; encourage clear liquids, especially electrolyte drinks, in uncomplicated labor. High-risk patients may need stricter limits; do not deny neuraxial analgesia solely for NPO status.

sources.name: Unscheduled Procedural Sedation Multidisciplinary Delphi Consensus Guidelines, Part 2: Clinical Practice
sources.accessNote: Full PDF read. Urgent or emergent procedures should not be delayed solely for fasting; assess the timing and nature of intake plus aspiration risk; refer moderate-risk patients for anesthesia care when available. This guidance is for unscheduled procedural sedation, not emergency general anesthesia.

sources.name: Derivation and prospective validation of a simple index for prediction of cardiac risk of major noncardiac surgery
scope: Revised Cardiac Risk Index: six predictors, definitions and rates by factor count (Table 3)
sources.accessNote: Full text read from the open eScholarship copy (2026-11-17). Table 3, validation cohort (n=1422): major cardiac complications 0.4%, 0.9%, 6.6%, 11.0% for 0, 1, 2, 3 or more factors; derivation cohort (n=2893): 0.5%, 1.3%, 3.6%, 9.1%. The abstract rounds the two-factor figures to 7% and 4%. High-risk surgery is intraperitoneal, intrathoracic or suprainguinal vascular. A 1999 single-centre cohort of patients aged 50 or over having elective major non-cardiac surgery.

sources.name: The post-anesthesia recovery score revisited (modified Aldrete score)

sources.name: Discharge criteria and complications after ambulatory surgery (revised PADSS)

The two books differ on the pain item: "not acceptable" scores 1 in Miller 6e and 0 in Clinical Cases.

sources.name: Validation of the 4AT, a new instrument for rapid delirium screening: a study in 234 hospitalised older people
sources.accessNote: Main text (open, PMC) and the supplementary 4AT form (version 1: item wording, points and bands) read in full on 2026-11-17. sources.name: Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine
sources.accessNote: Citation confirmed by web search (2026-11-17); the paper was not opened and PubMed blocked automated fetches. The formula and its SI constants (1.23 men, 1.04 women, creatinine in micromol/L) come from NKF and UK NHS summaries. This build uses ACTUAL body weight, as the DOAC trials and the US rivaroxaban label do according to secondary summaries (label not opened). The weight choice in obesity is contested: confirm against local protocol. Adults only: the paper studied patients aged 18 to 92.

scenarios.name: ARDS / lung-protective
cautions: Use predicted body weight (PBW), never actual body weight.
If plateau pressure stays above 30 cmH2O at 6 mL/kg PBW, consider reducing toward 4 mL/kg PBW.

scenarios.name: Normal adult (intraoperative)
cautions: The source gives a 6-8 mL/kg PBW range and a plateau below 28-30 cmH2O; it does not name a single target, so the lower bound is used as the starting point.
The 2019 expert consensus advises PEEP of 5 cmH2O or more, then individualized, and FiO2 0.4 after intubation, then the lowest FiO2 for SpO2 94% or higher. No preset default is supplied.

scenarios.name: Laparoscopic surgery
cautions: ESAIC/PROVE: Lung-protective ventilation (6-8 mL/kg PBW) and moderate PEEP (5-10 cmH2O) counteract cephalad diaphragm shift from pneumoperitoneum.
CO2 pneumoperitoneum lowers thoracopulmonary compliance and raises PaCO2 by 15-25% (plateauing at 20-30 min). Adjust minute ventilation to maintain normocapnia/permissive mild hypercapnia.

scenarios.name: Obesity / bariatric
cautions: PROBESE trial & ESPCOP: Tidal volume must be calculated strictly from PBW (7-8 mL/kg PBW), never actual weight.
Higher PEEP (8-12 cmH2O with recruitment maneuvers) maintains functional residual capacity in obese patients; titrate against driving pressure and hemodynamics.

scenarios.name: One-lung ventilation
cautions: ERAS/ESTS 2019: PEEP usually 5-10 cmH2O; FiO2 1.0 immediately before starting one-lung ventilation. The guideline gives no tidal volume, rate or I:E ratio.

scenarios.name: Pediatric
cautions: PALICC-2: In children without severe lung disease, target tidal volume 5-8 mL/kg based on ideal/predicted weight; plateau pressure limit <= 28 cmH2O (or <= 29-32 cmH2O with reduced chest wall compliance).
The adult Devine PBW formula is not valid for children.

scenarios.name: Obstetric
cautions: SOAP/OAA: Target tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg PBW with baseline PEEP 5 cmH2O.
Normal pregnancy has a baseline physiologic respiratory alkalosis (PaCO2 30-32 mmHg). Target EtCO2 around 30-32 mmHg to prevent severe maternal acidosis or fetal hypoperfusion.

modes.title: Volume control (VC)
points: Set tidal volume; pressure varies with compliance and resistance.

modes.title: Pressure control (PC)
points: Set inspiratory pressure; tidal volume varies. Watch delivered volume.

modes.title: Pressure support (PSV)
points: Patient-triggered, pressure-supported breaths; needs spontaneous effort and a backup plan.

modes.title: SIMV
points: Set mandatory breaths synchronized to patient effort, with spontaneous breaths between.

advancedReference.title: Baseline intraoperative IPPV (consensus)
points: Tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg predicted body weight (PBW), never actual weight.
Limit FiO2 to 0.6 or less where possible to reduce absorption atelectasis.
Respiratory rate 12-16 breaths/min (conventional IPPV: keep below 30/min).
PEEP baseline 5-10 cmH2O. Plateau pressure below 30 cmH2O. Driving pressure (plateau minus PEEP) below 14-15 cmH2O.

advancedReference.title: High-frequency and apneic modalities (Miller p. 1061, 1451)
points: HFPV: tidal volume 3-4 mL/kg at 60-100 breaths/min.
Thoracic HFV: tidal volume below 2 mL/kg at 60-2400 breaths/min.

Low-flow apneic oxygenation: 100% O2 with 5-10 cmH2O CPAP can maintain adequate PaO2 for at least 20 minutes, but PaCO2 rises about 6 mmHg in the first minute and 3-4 mmHg each minute after (reported PaCO2 103-250 mmHg, pH 6.72-6.97). The safe period is well below 10 minutes. Monitor SpO2.

advancedReference.title: Apneic threshold and laparoscopy (Miller p. 168, 1702)
points: Apneic threshold: the highest PaCO2 at which a patient stays apneic is 4-5 mmHg below the resting PaCO2.
CO2 pneumoperitoneum lowers thoracopulmonary compliance. PaCO2 rises by 15-25% and plateaus after 20-30 minutes.

advancedReference.title: One-lung ventilation (ERAS/ESTS & thoracic consensus)
points: FiO2 1.0 immediately before starting OLV; pressure control preferred; plateau pressure below 30 cmH2O; PEEP 5-10 cmH2O to the dependent lung and CPAP to the operative lung if hypoxemic.

advancedReference.title: Respiratory mechanics terms (Anesthesiology 2025, p. 1211)
points: Driving pressure = plateau pressure - PEEP.
Respiratory system compliance = tidal volume / (plateau pressure - PEEP).
Recruited volume: volume gained above the baseline compliance curve. Recruitment-to-inflation (R/I) ratio: assesses recruitability.
End-expiratory lung volume (EELV) and impedance (EELI): functional volume monitoring.
Breath phase variables: trigger, limit and cycle (pressure, volume, flow or time).

advancedReference.title: ARDS ventilation protocol (ARDSNet)
points: Start at 8 mL/kg predicted body weight, then reduce by 1 mL/kg at intervals of 2 hours or more to 6 mL/kg. Predicted body weight: men 50 + 2.3 x (height in inches - 60); women 45.5 + 2.3 x (height in inches - 60).

Plateau pressure goal 30 cmH2O or less. Set respiratory rate not above 35 breaths/min, starting near the baseline minute ventilation. Minimum PEEP 5 cmH2O. Inspiration is kept shorter than expiration; no numeric ratio is given.
Oxygenation goal: PaO2 55-80 mmHg or SpO2 88-95%.

advancedReference.title: Intraoperative lung-protective ventilation (2019 expert consensus)
points: Tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg predicted body weight (strong recommendation).
Start PEEP at 5 cmH2O or more, then individualize it.
FiO2 0.4 after intubation, then the lowest FiO2 that keeps SpO2 at 94% or higher (weak recommendation).
No respiratory rate, I:E ratio or ventilation mode is recommended: the panel found the evidence lacking.

advancedReference.title: FiO2 during general anesthesia: guidance differs
points: WHO 2016: 80% FiO2 intraoperatively for adults under general anesthesia with intubation, and if feasible for 2-6 hours afterwards (a strong recommendation in 2016; reported as changed to conditional in the 2018 update).
The 2019 lung-protective consensus advises 0.4 after intubation, then the lowest FiO2 for SpO2 94% or higher. The two disagree, so no default is set here.

advancedReference.title: One-lung ventilation (ERAS/ESTS 2019)
points: PEEP is usually in the range of 5-10 cmH2O.
FiO2 1.0 immediately before starting one-lung ventilation speeds collapse of the non-ventilated lung.
Lowering tidal volume from the traditional 10 mL/kg ideal body weight to 4-6 mL/kg is described as likely less injurious; large trials are lacking.
No respiratory rate, I:E ratio or plateau limit is given.

advancedReference.title: Obesity: PROBESE trial settings (a trial protocol, not a recommendation)
points: Tidal volume 7 mL/kg predicted body weight, volume control, I:E 1:2.
PEEP 12 cmH2O with recruitment maneuvers versus 4 cmH2O without.
Respiratory rate adjusted for end-tidal CO2 35-45 mmHg; FiO2 at least 0.4 with SpO2 above 92%.
Recruitment: tidal volume raised in 4 mL/kg steps until plateau pressure reaches 40-50 cmH2O, held for 3 breaths; peak pressure limit 55 cmH2O.

alarms.title: High airway pressure
points: Treat as a real problem until excluded: check the patient, circuit and tube.

alarms.title: Low airway pressure / disconnection
points: Check the circuit connections, the cuff and the machine.

alarms.title: Low or high minute ventilation
points: Compare with your set tidal volume and rate; look for leak, obstruction or patient effort.

alarms.title: Apnea
points: Confirm capnography waveform and chest movement; start manual ventilation if absent.

troubleshooting.title: High airway pressure
points: Disconnect and hand-ventilate to separate a patient problem from a machine problem.
Think: tube position or kink, secretions, bronchospasm, pneumothorax, abdominal or positioning cause, depth of block.

troubleshooting.title: Low tidal volume
points: Check for leak (cuff, circuit, mask), disconnection, or a mode change.

troubleshooting.title: Hypoxemia
points: Give 100% oxygen and confirm ventilation; check tube position and the circuit before other causes.

troubleshooting.title: Hypercapnia
points: Check minute ventilation, circuit and absorbent; consider increased CO2 production.

troubleshooting.title: Circuit leak
points: Leak-test the circuit and check the cuff; use a self-inflating bag as backup.

troubleshooting.title: Auto-PEEP
points: Look for an expiratory flow that does not return to zero; allow longer expiration and disconnect briefly if the patient is unstable.

lastSteps.text: Stop injecting local anesthetic. Call for help. Get the lipid emulsion / LAST kit.
Manage the airway and ventilate with 100% oxygen.

lastSteps.note: Propofol is not a substitute for lipid emulsion.

lastSteps.text: Give 20% lipid emulsion bolus (dose from the calculator below for this weight).
Start the 20% lipid emulsion infusion (dose from the calculator below).
lastSteps.note: Continue for at least 10 minutes after hemodynamic stability.

lastSteps.text: If cardiac arrest: follow ACLS with LAST modifications. Reduce epinephrine doses. Avoid vasopressin, calcium channel blockers, beta blockers and further local anesthetic.
lastSteps.note: Use the ASRA checklist for the epinephrine dose; do not rely on local anesthetic-related interventions alone.

lastSteps.text: If instability continues: repeat the lipid bolus and double the infusion rate (do not exceed the cumulative ceiling).
Alert the nearest facility with cardiopulmonary bypass / ECMO capability early if refractory.

mhSteps.text: Stop all volatile anesthetics and succinylcholine.
Call for help and declare an MH emergency. Get the MH cart / dantrolene.
Hyperventilate with 100% oxygen at high flow.
Give dantrolene IV (initial dose from the calculator below, on actual body weight).
Repeat dantrolene until signs of MH are controlled. Track the cumulative dose.
mhSteps.note: Both product labels cite 10 mg/kg as the maximum cumulative dose.

mhSteps.text: Treat hyperkalemia and acidosis per the MHAUS / EMHG protocol.
Treat arrhythmias per the MHAUS / EMHG protocol.
Monitor temperature, end-tidal CO2, blood gases, potassium and urine output.
Contact your MH hotline / local MH contact (set in Settings).

cicoPlans.title: Plan A: Tracheal intubation

steps.text: Preoxygenate and keep oxygenating throughout (supplemental oxygen).
Optimize each attempt (position, device, operator). Limit the number of attempts.
After intubation, confirm placement with capnography (waveform end-tidal CO2).

failureCriteria: Tracheal intubation not achieved within your attempt limit
Oxygenation falling or cannot be maintained

cicoPlans.title: Plan B: Alternative intubation technique or supraglottic airway

steps.text: Use an alternative technique or place a supraglottic airway. Limit attempts.

failureCriteria: Ventilation or oxygenation not achieved through the alternative device

cicoPlans.title: Plan C: Face-mask ventilation / rescue oxygenation

steps.text: Optimize face-mask ventilation (two-person technique, adjuncts). Consider waking the patient if feasible.
Call for help now if not already done.

failureCriteria: Cannot oxygenate or ventilate by any non-invasive route: declare CICO and go to Plan D without delay

steps.text: Declare "Can't intubate, can't oxygenate" and call for the invasive airway kit.
Perform invasive airway access without delay, using the technique you are trained in and your local kit.

checklists.title: Fasting / NPO
checklists.note: Draft for clinician review. Times are minimum fasting intervals before anesthesia or sedation for healthy elective patients; special scenarios and local protocols change them. Avoid routine NPO after midnight. GLP-1 guidance conflicts: use one locally adopted protocol, not a mix.

items.text: Record the time, type and amount of last oral intake, procedure urgency and aspiration risk. Fasting does not guarantee an empty stomach.
Solid food / light meal: at least 6 h. Large, fatty, fried or meat-containing meals: at least 8 h; assess amount and type.
Non-clear liquids: at least 6 h, including milk, milk products, meal-replacement drinks and enteral formulas.

Clear liquids: until 2 h before anesthesia or sedation. Examples: water, pulp-free clear juice, tea/coffee, lemonade, clear carbohydrate drinks; no alcohol. The 2026 international consensus counts tea/coffee with milk up to one-fifth of total volume as clear; otherwise follow the local definition.
Clear liquids <2 h, including "Sip Til Send": only under an explicit institutional protocol; not an individual clinician shortcut.

Healthy adults: simple or complex carbohydrate clear liquids may be taken until 2 h; up to 400 mL is considered an appropriate volume (ASA 2023). Protein-added clear liquids are not preferred for lack of evidence; do not confuse them with milk or meal-replacement drinks, which need 6 h.
Gum or lollipops may be used until transfer under the 2026 adult consensus, but remove before induction or sedation. Do not delay a healthy adult solely because of gum (ASA 2023).
Children: allow clear liquids as close to 2 h as possible. ASA 2023 found insufficient evidence to choose 1 h over 2 h; use a shorter interval only under a pediatric protocol or clinical judgment.
Neonates and infants: breast milk for at least 4 h.
Infants: formula or nonhuman milk for at least 6 h.
Enteral feeding: at least 6 h, but preprocedural discontinuation is not required for most patients with an already secure airway (for example, cuffed tracheostomy or tracheal tube in situ).

Do not apply healthy-patient intervals automatically with: significant uncontrolled reflux or supine regurgitation, hiatal hernia, Zenker diverticulum, achalasia or stricture; previous gastric surgery; gastroparesis; diabetes; end-stage kidney disease; opioid use; GI obstruction or acute abdomen; pregnancy; obesity; frailty/comorbidity; emergency status. Individualize the aspiration plan.
Obesity or previous gastric/bariatric surgery: individualize fasting and aspiration risk; gastric ultrasound may be technically harder after gastric surgery.

GLP-1 RA or tirzepatide: document drug, dose, schedule, last dose, escalation phase, GI symptoms and other delayed-emptying risks. Most patients continue therapy rather than routinely withholding it; use the locally adopted protocol.

GLP-1 escalation phase or significant GI symptoms: defer elective care until resolved (2024 multisociety). SPAQI 2025 defines significant as severe nausea, vomiting or inability to tolerate oral intake (not fullness or early satiety) and requires prescriber review before elective care.

Higher GLP-1 dose or another cause of delayed emptying: consider a 24 h liquid-only diet, aspiration-plan changes and trained gastric ultrasound; delay in selected cases when risk is expected to decrease (2024 multisociety).

If the SPAQI 2025 protocol is locally adopted: continue GLP-1 RA if there are no significant GI symptoms; solids 24 h (clear liquids only); clear liquids <10% glucose 4 h and ≥10% glucose 8 h. Do not mix these times with another GLP-1 protocol.
Uncomplicated elective cesarean or obstetric surgery: moderate clear liquids until 2 h; solids 6-8 h depending on fat content (ASA 2016).

Active labor: avoid solid food; encourage clear liquids, especially electrolyte-containing drinks, in uncomplicated labor. High-risk patients may need stricter limits, and never deny neuraxial analgesia or anesthesia solely for NPO status.
Emergency or urgent anesthesia: elective minimums do not apply automatically. Document last intake, assess aspiration risk and let urgency plus the anesthesia plan determine any delay.

Unscheduled procedural sedation: assess timing and nature of intake plus aspiration risk; do not delay urgent or emergent procedures solely for fasting. Refer moderate-risk patients for prompt anesthesia care when available (ACEP 2026).
Gastric ultrasound: a trained provider may use it when additional information would change management; do not treat it as routine screening or a guarantee of an empty stomach.
Bowel preparation or a procedure requiring specific gastric conditions: follow the procedure-specific diet and fasting instructions; routine intervals are not a substitute.

checklists.title: Anesthesia machine / breathing system
checklists.note: Use your institutional checklist. This is a generic structure only and contains no device-specific steps.

items.text: Institutional pre-use checklist completed
Power and gas supply confirmed
Breathing system assembled and leak-tested
Ventilator working
Scavenging connected
Monitors and alarms working
Backup means of ventilation available
Positioning and pressure points
Temperature
Fluids
Blood loss
Neuromuscular blockade monitoring
Antibiotic redosing due?
Ventilation checks
Vasopressor and infusion checks
Reversal given or blockade resolved
Adequate spontaneous ventilation
Adequate oxygenation
Airway protective reflexes present
Hemodynamically stable
Temperature acceptable
Suction available
Extubation risk factors identified

checklists.title: Pre-case "two-bag" test (AAGBI 2012)
checklists.note: Do this after the breathing system, vaporisers and ventilator have been checked individually (Fundamentals of Anesthesia 4e, Ch 46, p. 905). Follow your institutional checklist for your machine.

items.text: Attach the patient end of the breathing system (including angle piece and filter) to a test lung or bag
Set fresh gas flow to 5 L/min and ventilate manually. Check the whole breathing system is patent and the unidirectional valves are moving. Check the APL valve by squeezing both bags
Turn on the ventilator to ventilate the test lung. Turn off the fresh gas flow, or reduce it to a minimum. Open and close each vaporiser in turn. There should be no loss of volume in the system

checklists.title: Pre-case ventilator check (FDA 1993 excerpts)
checklists.note: Excerpts from the FDA 1993 apparatus checkout (step 12 ventilator test, step 13 monitors). The vaporizer interlock, fit, fill and leak item was transcribed earlier and was not located in the notebook text retrieved: confirm it against the full checkout. Follow your institutional checklist for your machine.

items.text: Attach a second breathing bag to the Y-piece
Ventilator ON: bellows deliver the appropriate tidal volume on inspiration and fill completely on expiration
Verify unidirectional valves, vaporizer interlocks, and vaporizer fit, fill and leaks
Check and calibrate the capnometer and O2 analyzer

checklists.title: ASA basic monitoring standards
checklists.note: Transcribed from the project notebook (Miller 6e p. 2027).

items.text: Qualified anesthesia personnel continuously present
Oxygenation: inspired O2 low-limit alarm and SpO2
Ventilation: ETCO2 and disconnect alarm
Circulation: ECG and NIBP at intervals of 5 minutes at most
Temperature evaluated

checklists.title: Non-operating-room anesthesia (NORA / MRI)
checklists.note: Transcribed from the project notebook (Miller 6e p. 2025).

items.text: Dedicated reliable O2 source plus a full backup cylinder
Reliable suction and scavenging
Full ASA monitors and a self-inflating hand resuscitator bag (AMBU)
MR Safe / MR Conditional / MR Unsafe status verified for all equipment

checklists.title: Airway management plan
checklists.note: Principles from the ASA 2022 difficult airway guideline as already shown on the Airway tab. If oxygenation fails, open SOS > CICO for Plans A-D.

items.text: Device sizes chosen and checked for this patient (Airway tab)
Preoxygenate and keep supplemental oxygen going throughout airway management
Confirm tracheal intubation with capnography
Limit repeated attempts at any one technique; track time and oxygen saturation
Escalate early when ventilation or oxygenation fails; do not delay invasive airway access when CICO is declared

checklists.title: Lung-protective setup
checklists.note: Intraoperative settings from the 2019 international expert consensus. It recommends no respiratory rate, I:E ratio or mode. Use the Vent tab for the tidal volume in mL.

items.text: Tidal volume set from predicted body weight, never actual weight (Vent tab)
Tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg predicted body weight
PEEP started at 5 cmH2O or more, then individualized
FiO2 0.4 after intubation, then the lowest FiO2 that keeps SpO2 at 94% or higher
Plateau pressure below 30 cmH2O; driving pressure (plateau minus PEEP) below 14-15 cmH2O

checklists.title: One-lung ventilation
checklists.note: From the ERAS/ESTS 2019 lung surgery guideline, which gives no respiratory rate, I:E ratio or plateau limit and notes that large trials of low tidal volume are lacking.

items.text: FiO2 1.0 immediately before starting one-lung ventilation (speeds collapse of the non-ventilated lung)
Tidal volume lowered towards 4-6 mL/kg ideal body weight (described as likely less injurious than the traditional 10 mL/kg)
PEEP usually in the range of 5-10 cmH2O

checklists.title: High airway pressure
checklists.note: Generic troubleshooting prompts, as on the Vent tab. Treat the alarm as a real problem until excluded.

items.text: Disconnect and hand-ventilate to separate a patient problem from a machine problem
Tube position or kink, and secretions, checked
Bronchospasm and pneumothorax considered
Abdominal or positioning cause, and depth of block, considered
Auto-PEEP: expiratory flow returns to zero; if not, allow longer expiration and disconnect briefly if unstable

checklists.title: Hypoxemia on the ventilator
checklists.note: Generic troubleshooting prompts, as on the Vent tab.

items.text: Give 100% oxygen and confirm ventilation (capnography waveform and chest movement)
Tube position and the circuit checked before other causes
Leak or disconnection excluded (cuff, circuit, mask); self-inflating bag available as backup
No waveform or chest movement: start manual ventilation

checklists.title: Local anesthetic dose check
checklists.note: Use Dosing > Local anesthetics for the maximum in mg for this patient. If toxicity is suspected, open SOS > LAST.

items.text: Maximum dose worked out for this agent and weight, plain or with epinephrine, before drawing up
More than one local anesthetic: the fractions of each maximum add up to less than 1.0
Total cumulative local anesthetic dose discussed with the team and documented
Lidocaine by continuous epidural or caudal: maximum dose not repeated at intervals under 90 minutes
Location of the 20% lipid emulsion / LAST kit known

checklists.title: Spinal / epidural preparation
checklists.note: Generic structure only; follow your institutional neuraxial and anticoagulation policy. Reference regimens are for a 70 kg adult as printed and are never scaled by weight.

items.text: Consent, indication and contraindications reviewed
Coagulation status and anticoagulant timing checked against local policy
IV access, monitoring, oxygen, suction and resuscitation drugs ready
Agent, concentration, volume and baricity checked against a reference regimen (Dosing tab)
Aseptic technique and drug labels confirmed

checklists.title: Anaphylaxis
checklists.note: Adapted from QRH 3-1 Anaphylaxis v5 (2022). Adrenaline doses are the QRH figures; ANZAAG-ANZCA gives graded doses (see the epinephrine reference on the Dosing tab). Follow your local protocol. Cardiac arrest: follow your arrest algorithm.

items.text: Call for help and note the time. Stop or do not start non-essential surgery
Send for the cardiac arrest trolley, anaphylaxis treatment pack and investigation pack
Remove possible triggers (antibiotics, neuromuscular blockers, patent blue, chlorhexidine, IV colloids). Maintain anaesthesia; change to an inhalational agent
Give 100% oxygen and ensure adequate ventilation; secure the airway with a tracheal tube if needed
Elevate the legs if hypotensive
Systolic pressure below 50 mmHg or cardiac arrest: start CPR immediately
Adrenaline, adult: IV 50 mcg (0.5 mL of 1:10 000), repeat as necessary; IM 0.5 mg (0.5 mL of 1:1000) if IV is not possible. Child: IV 1 mcg/kg (0.1 mL/kg of 1:100 000)
Consider an adrenaline infusion after three boluses (adult: 3 mg in 50 mL saline, start at 3 mL/h, titrate to a maximum of 40 mL/h)

Resistant hypotension: add another vasopressor (e.g. metaraminol, noradrenaline infusion, vasopressin adult 2 units repeated as necessary). Beta-blocked and unresponsive to adrenaline: glucagon adult 1 mg, repeat as necessary
Rapid IV crystalloid: 20 mL/kg initial bolus, repeated until hypotension resolves
Persistent bronchospasm: open the Bronchospasm list
Serum tryptase: 5-10 mL clotted blood as soon as the patient is stable; repeat at 1-2 hours and after 24 hours
Hydrocortisone and chlorphenamine are not part of acute treatment; consider steroids afterwards for refractory reactions or ongoing asthma/shock
Plan transfer to critical care; mark the allergy (band, notes, drug chart); arrange allergy referral and inform the patient and team

checklists.title: Massive blood loss
checklists.note: Adapted from QRH 3-2 Massive blood loss v2 (2018). This page has not been updated since 2018: use your local major haemorrhage protocol where its triggers or targets differ.

items.text: Call for help, tell the theatre team and note the time
Increase FiO2; consider cautiously reducing anaesthetic agents
Check and expose IV access
Control obvious bleeding (pressure, uterotonics, tourniquet, haemostatic dressings)
Call the blood bank and activate the major haemorrhage protocol; say how fast and how much. Assign one person to liaise
Start active patient warming; use rapid infusion and fluid warming equipment

Agree the plan with surgical and nursing teams; consider interventional radiology and cell salvage; involve a haematologist for anticoagulants, bleeding disorders or uncontrolled non-surgical bleeding
Monitor with point-of-care tests (Hb, lactate, coagulation) and lab tests including calcium and fibrinogen
Goals as printed (2018): Hb above 80 g/L; platelets above 75 x 10^9/L; PT and APTT below 1.5 x control; fibrinogen above 1.0 g/L; avoid acidosis, hypothermia, hypocalcaemia and hyperkalaemia
Calcium, adult: 10 mL of 10% calcium chloride IV or 20 mL of 10% calcium gluconate IV. Child: 0.2 mL/kg chloride or 0.5 mL/kg gluconate
Consider tranexamic acid, adult: 1 g IV bolus, then 1 g over 8 hours (obstetric: repeat 1 g after 30 minutes instead). Child: 15 mg/kg then 2 mg/kg/h
Plan ongoing care in an appropriate clinical area

checklists.title: Bronchospasm
checklists.note: Adapted from QRH 3-4 Bronchospasm v3 (2023). Only first-line doses are listed here; the QRH page gives doses for ipratropium, adrenaline, ketamine, aminophylline and hydrocortisone.

items.text: Call for help and tell the theatre team
Give 100% oxygen. Stop surgery and other stimulation
Expose and examine the chest. No wheeze may mean severe bronchospasm with no air movement
Deepen anaesthesia; avoid rapid increases of isoflurane or desflurane
Exclude mimics: mispositioned or blocked airway device, endobronchial or oesophageal intubation, blocked breathing system, pneumothorax, pulmonary oedema, laryngospasm
Consider anaphylaxis; if suspected open the Anaphylaxis list
First line: salbutamol by inhaler or nebuliser (adult and over 5 years 5 mg; under 5 years 2.5 mg). Remove the HME filter or nebulise downstream of it
Second line: salbutamol IV, adult 250 mcg diluted and given slowly. Magnesium IV 50 mg/kg (adult 2 g) over 20 minutes. Other drugs at clinician discretion
Suspected aspiration: consider intubation and tracheal toilet; aspirate the stomach by nasogastric tube
Ventilation: lengthen expiratory time, watch for breath stacking, consider pressure control and permissive hypercapnia
Chest X-ray when safe; plan post-procedure care

checklists.title: Laryngospasm
checklists.note: Adapted from QRH 3-6 Laryngospasm and stridor v1 (2018). A correctly positioned tracheal tube rules out laryngospasm.

items.text: Call for help and tell the theatre team
Jaw thrust; stop all other stimulation
Remove airway devices and anything stimulating or blocking the airway (suction catheter, blood, vomit); look and suction if in doubt
CPAP with 100% oxygen by face mask. Avoid forceful inflation (it fills the stomach). Add an oral or nasal airway if the upper airway may not be clear
If it persists: continue CPAP, deepen anaesthesia, give a neuromuscular blocker
Doses as printed: 0.25-0.5 mg/kg IV of propofol, rocuronium, atracurium or suxamethonium; suxamethonium IM (including tongue) 4 mg/kg
Consider tracheal intubation, especially if likely to recur
Decompress the stomach with a nasogastric tube
Consider other causes: foreign body, infection, anaphylaxis, tumour, vocal cord paralysis, airway obstruction or compression
Plan a safe wake-up; continued support may be needed after aspiration or negative-pressure pulmonary oedema

items.label: High-risk surgery (intraperitoneal, intrathoracic or suprainguinal vascular)

items.label: Snoring: do you snore loudly (louder than talking, or heard through a closed door)?
Tired: do you often feel tired, fatigued or sleepy in the daytime?
Observed: has anyone seen you stop breathing during sleep?
Pressure: do you have, or are you treated for, high blood pressure?

bands.label: Intermediate risk

bands.detail: Postoperative nausea and vomiting occurs in approximately 10% of patients with no risk factor.

bands.label: High risk

choiceScores.name: Modified Aldrete score (PACU discharge)

options.label: Moves all extremities voluntarily or on command

items.label: Circulation
items.prompt: Textbooks differ: Clinical Cases in Anesthesia gives these bands in percent; Miller 6e prints them as ± 20, 20 to 50 and 50 mm of the pre-anesthetic level. Use your unit's form if it differs.

options.label: Blood pressure within ± 20% of the pre-anesthetic level
Blood pressure ± 20% to 50% of the pre-anesthetic level
Blood pressure more than ± 50% from the pre-anesthetic level

items.label: Oxygen saturation
items.prompt: Textbooks differ on 0 points: this is the Clinical Cases in Anesthesia wording; Miller 6e prints "SpO2 below 92% with oxygen", which overlaps its own 1-point level.

options.label: Needs supplemental oxygen to keep SpO2 above 90%

bands.label: Below the discharge mark
bands.detail: Fewer than 9 of 10.

bands.label: Meets the discharge mark
bands.detail: 9 or more of 10 ("at least 9 out of 10", Miller 6e). The score supports the discharge decision; it does not make it.

choiceScores.note: The 1995 modification of the Aldrete score replaced skin colour with pulse oximetry. The 1995 letter could not be read, so the wording comes from two textbooks, which differ on the two items marked above. Check your local PACU discharge form.
choiceScores.why: Five signs (activity, breathing, blood pressure, consciousness and oxygen saturation) are each scored 0 to 2; 9 or more of 10 suggests the patient can leave the PACU.

choiceScores.name: PADSS (home readiness after day surgery)

options.label: More than 40% from the preoperative baseline
Steady gait, no dizziness (or meets the preoperative level)

items.label: Pain
items.prompt: Pain should be acceptable to the patient and controllable with oral analgesics, and its location, type and intensity consistent with the expected discomfort. Textbooks differ on "not acceptable": Clinical Cases in Anesthesia gives 0 points, Miller 6e gives 1.

options.label: Moderate: up to two dressing changes
Severe: more than three dressing changes

bands.label: Not yet home-ready by score
bands.detail: Fewer than 9 of 10.

bands.label: Home-ready by score
bands.detail: 9 or more of 10, with an adult escort (Miller 6e). The score supports the discharge decision; it does not make it.

choiceScores.note: This is the revised PADSS (Marshall and Chung 1999), as both textbooks print it, with pain scored as acceptable or not. Voiding before discharge is no longer required, except after genitourinary, gynecologic, or inguinal or perineal surgery. The two textbooks differ on the item marked above. Check your local discharge policy.
choiceScores.why: Five criteria (vital signs, walking, nausea and vomiting, pain and bleeding) are each scored 0 to 2; 9 or more of 10 suggests readiness to go home after day surgery.

choiceScores.name: 4AT delirium screen

items.label: Alertness
items.prompt: This includes patients who may be markedly drowsy (eg. difficult to rouse and/or obviously sleepy during assessment) or agitated/hyperactive. Observe the patient. If asleep, attempt to wake with speech or gentle touch on shoulder. Ask the patient to state their name and address to assist rating.

options.label: Normal (fully alert, but not agitated, throughout assessment)
Mild sleepiness for <10 seconds after waking, then normal

items.label: AMT4
items.prompt: Age, date of birth, place (name of the hospital or building), current year.

items.label: Attention
items.prompt: Ask the patient: "Please tell me the months of the year in backwards order, starting at December." To assist initial understanding one prompt of "what is the month before December?" is permitted.

options.label: Starts but scores < 7 months / refuses to start
Untestable (cannot start because unwell, drowsy, inattentive)

items.label: Acute change or fluctuating course
items.prompt: Evidence of significant change or fluctuation in: alertness, cognition, other mental function (eg. paranoia, hallucinations) arising over the last 2 weeks and still evident in last 24hrs.

bands.label: Delirium or cognitive impairment unlikely
bands.detail: But delirium is still possible if the acute change item (4) information is incomplete.

bands.label: Possible cognitive impairment
bands.detail: A score of 1 to 3.

bands.label: Possible delirium +/- cognitive impairment
bands.detail: A score of 4 or above.

choiceScores.note: A screening instrument, not a diagnosis: a score of 4 or more suggests delirium, and more detailed assessment of mental status may be required. Items 1 to 3 are rated on observation of the patient at the time of assessment. Item 4 needs information from one or more sources (for example your own knowledge of the patient, other staff, case notes, carers). Take account of hearing impairment, dysphasia and lack of a common language. It was validated in hospitalised patients aged 70 or over, not specifically after surgery. This is version 1 of the form; check www.the4AT.com for the current one.
choiceScores.why: Four quick items (alertness, a short memory test, attention, and any recent change) add up to 0 to 12. A score of 4 or more flags possible delirium.
